title: Affine values of the functions-modulo-constant-sheaf quotient
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $A$ an abelian group. On the small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the presheaf $\operatorname{fun}(-,A)$ sending $V\to X$ to all set maps $|V|\to A$, with restrictions by precomposition, is a sheaf of abelian groups. Let $\underline A$ be the constant abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Locally constant functions induce a monomorphism $\underline A\to\operatorname{fun}(-,A)$. Let $\mathcal Q_A$ be its cokernel in abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], equivalently the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of its presheaf cokernel. If every point of $X$ is closed (its singleton is closed) and has separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed] residue field $\kappa(x)=\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x$ [def-weil-residue-field], then for every affine object $V\to X$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$\mathcal Q_A(V)\cong\frac{\operatorname{Map}(|V|,A)}{\operatorname{LC}(|V|,A)},$$
where $|V|$ is the underlying topological space, and $\operatorname{LC}(|V|,A)$ is the subgroup of functions which are constant on an open neighbourhood of each point.

proof.text: Give $A$ the indiscrete topology. Every map $|U|\to A$ is continuous, and addition and negation are continuous, since every map into an indiscrete space is continuous. Apply [lem-cbc-continuous-functions-fpqc-sheaf]. Every pro-etale covering is an fpqc covering by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], so the equalizer condition for these coverings gives exactly the sheaf condition for $\operatorname{fun}(-,A)$. With the discrete topology on $A$, the same cited lemma gives a sheaf $L(U)=\operatorname{LC}(|U|,A)$: continuity into a discrete space is equivalent to each point having a neighbourhood of constant value. The pointwise operations make $L$ an abelian subsheaf of $\operatorname{fun}(-,A)$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12 (continuous-map sheaf); 0F6D, first sentence for fun

proof.text: The constant-presheaf map to discrete-valued continuous functions is locally surjective: cover by the open fibres, indexed by points of the object to stay in universe u. It is locally injective: unequal constants can agree only on the empty scheme, which has the empty cover. The sheafification map is therefore an isomorphism by Mathlib locally-bijective sheafification. Inclusion into all functions is pointwise injective, and its range consists exactly of locally constant functions. This identifies [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] with that subsheaf, with the specified unit compatibility.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, last assertion, with universal-property argument written out

proof.text: The abelian-sheaf cokernel exists by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The sheafification of the presheaf cokernel is that cokernel: [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact] says sheafification preserves colimits. More explicitly maps from the presheaf cokernel to a sheaf $G$ are precisely maps $\operatorname{fun}(-,A)\to G$ annihilating $\underline A$, and its sheafification has the same maps by adjunction. Together with the monomorphism from step 2 this yields the short exact sequence $0\to\underline A\to\operatorname{fun}(-,A)\to\mathcal Q_A\to0$.

source.place: Tag 0F6D, displayed short exact sequence; Sites 00WH, 00WJ

proof.text: Base-change a weakly etale map to the residue field of a point. On an affine open of its fibre the coordinate algebra is weakly etale over that field. The source absolutely-flat API (Algebra.WeaklyEtale.flat_lmul' and Ring.AbsolutelyFlat.of_flat_lmul') implies every prime is maximal, so the affine open is T1. By [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field] each residue field is separable over the base field and hence equal to it by Mathlib IsSepClosed.algebraMap_bijective. Transfer separable closedness along the resulting ring isomorphisms. Specializations share an affine neighbourhood, so the whole fibre is T1. Since the base point is closed, its residue-field map and its base change are closed immersions. A closed immersion carries closed fibre points to closed points. Surjectivity of its stalk maps makes its maps on residue fields bijective, transferring separable closedness to the original scheme.

source.place: Tag 0F6D, sentence that all points of U are closed with separably closed residue fields; More on Algebra 092Q and 092R

proof.text: Use the declared comparisonConstantSheafIso and comparisonCohomologyMap_bijective in [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison], and apply [lem-cbc-affine-sepclosed-etale-acyclic] to the affine object with the geometric properties from step 4. Thus the pro-etale constant sheaf on the object has vanishing H1. Use the already proved sliceEquiv and sliceDense in [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] to identify its site with the slice of the base site. ConstantSheafOver and ConstantSheafEquivalence transport the constant sheaf through this equivalence, and the proved source H.mapFunctor_bijective transports H1 vanishing.

source.place: Tag 0F6D, vanishing display and preceding constant-pullback sentence; 099W(1), 09AY; 03F3 for localization

proof.text: Restrict the cokernel short exact sequence directly to the slice at the affine object. The restriction preserves finite limits and colimits, hence the sequence remains short exact. At the terminal object of the slice the connecting map into H1 of the restricted constant sheaf is zero by step 5. The source lemma Sheaf.H.ker_δ, proved from the Ext exact sequence, identifies its kernel with the range of the cokernel projection; thus that projection is surjective on sections. Left exactness of evaluation identifies its kernel with the image of the constant sheaf, which is exactly the locally constant functions by step 2. QuotientAddGroup.quotientKerEquivOfSurjective gives the stated equivalence and the required formula by reflexivity. No generic derived-functor comparison or object-cohomology localization theorem is used.

source.place: Tag 0F6D, final displayed affine quotient formula; Derived Categories 015B
